$comment: D-FULLC-STDBIT-BIG-ENDIAN-NATIVE: the runnable coherence witness for C23 7.18.2's endianness macros, and the example the `charIsUnsigned` precedent demands whenever one fact acquires a second notation. THE CHANGE IT PINS: `shippedLibs/stdbit.json` carried `__STDC_ENDIAN_NATIVE__` as the literal 1234 from 2026-07-15; it now names `__BYTE_ORDER__`, the per-CPU predefine every `<arch>.target.json` already declares (D-PP-ENDIANNESS-PREDEFINES / TF-C115). ★ WHY A CORRECT ANSWER STILL NEEDED FIXING: every DSS target is little-endian, so the literal was RIGHT — right the way a hardcoded constant is right, by coincidence of the current target set, with nothing that would make the person adding a big-endian target look inside a header descriptor. ★★ THE FALSIFIABILITY IS TWO-AXIS, AND THE ONE-AXIS VERSION IS VACUOUS — ✔MEASURED, and an earlier draft of this manifest claimed the opposite. A C preprocessor compares macro VALUES and cannot inspect a replacement LIST, so on a little-endian target the derivation and the literal 1234 are INDISTINGUISHABLE: reverting stdbit.json to the literal leaves this example GREEN on every shipped leg. The second axis is what makes the difference visible — mutate the TARGET's `__BYTE_ORDER__` to `__ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__` (and `__LITTLE_ENDIAN__` to `__BIG_ENDIAN__`, which is what a real big-endian target would declare). FULL MATRIX, all four cells ✔MEASURED 2026-08-26 through DSS_CONFIG_ROOT against isolated config copies, the live checkout byte-identical throughout: [derived + LITTLE] BUILT, exit 77. [literal + LITTLE] BUILT — the invisible cell, and the reason a single-axis mutant proves nothing here. [derived + BIG] REFUSED, `LEG 3: no shipped DSS target is big-endian` — i.e. NATIVE FOLLOWED the target, which IS the derivation, observed. [literal + BIG] REFUSED, `LEG 2: __STDC_ENDIAN_NATIVE__ must BE the target's __BYTE_ORDER__, not a literal that happens to match it today` — i.e. the PRE-CHANGE config caught in the act of reporting little-endian on a big-endian machine. Cells 3 and 4 together are the close: one shows the fix working, the other shows exactly what it fixed. ★ THE ROW'S STATED CLOSING WORK WAS NOT NEEDED, and measuring that is what closed it: the row called for 'a per-target macro channel (a .target.json predefined-macro surface, or an endianness knob threaded into the shipped-macro splice)', and ✔MEASURED 2026-08-26 that channel had ALREADY SHIPPED — arm64.target.json declares 7 predefined macros and x86_64 6, including `__BYTE_ORDER__` whose value is itself a macro REFERENCE. What was missing was only stdbit.json REFERENCING it. A per-target `when` was never the route and could not have been: ✔MEASURED, shipped-lib macro `when` variants are FORMAT-ONLY (`matchVariantWhen` under `WhenAxes::FormatOnly`, which makes an `arch` key a hard load error) and the splice takes no arch parameter at all (`readShippedLibMacros(path, reporter, activeFormat)`). A macro REFERENCE crosses that layer with zero plumbing. ★ THIS IS WHAT THE REFERENCES DO, MEASURED SEPARATELY: gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 18.1.3, `-dM -E` after `#include <stdbit.h>`, both report `#define __STDC_ENDIAN_NATIVE__ __BYTE_ORDER` — glibc derives it too. And `s390x-linux-gnu-gcc` reports `__BYTE_ORDER__ __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__` with `__ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__` 4321, which is byte-identical to C23's `__STDC_ENDIAN_BIG__` — so on the s390x target plan 23 FC19 will land, the derived NATIVE is already the right answer with no edit to this file. WHAT IT COVERS THAT `endianness_predefines` DOES NOT: that example proves the TARGET and LANGUAGE layers resolve against each other; this one adds the SHIPPED-LIBRARY layer on top, so the value crosses three config layers and two rescans before it is an integer. LEG BRACKETING: legs 3 and 4 assert NATIVE is not BIG and IS LITTLE, so a NATIVE that resolved to 0 — the value C 6.10.1p4 gives an undefined identifier, and the silent failure this macro family has produced before — fails BOTH rather than passing leg 3 by accident. FOLD-RESISTANCE / RUNTIME: `endianWitness()` reads the low byte of a `volatile unsigned` through a `char` lens, so the runtime arm reports the byte order the CODE GENERATOR produced independently of the macro table, and it is MULTIPLIED into the exit code — a macro table that disagreed with the emitted code cannot exit 77. The `release` arm runs the shipped release pipeline over the same source so optimizer x feature composition is witnessed rather than assumed.
